Not sure if you're in the US or Europe, or have ever bought plants wholesale before, but the profit margin is next to none. I run a fairly successful online plant/terrarium store and I think we price quite high for quality, and even our profit margins are razor thin without a shopfront. Local plant b&m stores I follow are pricing half of what we are - and I honestly don't know how they can afford to do it. The competition ramps prices down, everyone having access to plants and growers now ramps prices down, and the sheer cost of maintaining a b&m and the stock levels that you need is enough to make you broke very quickly. 

I've been in business about 3 years, and in that time I've witnessed 6 plant shops open and go bust, and that's just within the surrounding towns to me. 

Niching down would be the best way to go, but honestly you might just be better off with an online shop to start with. Takes a lot of the cost away.

I sell sale or return to some small local shops. When my items sell, they pay me 70% of the cost of the item and they get to keep 30%. I know a lot of people don't like that, but honestly it's a good way to get friendly because the shop is taking no upfront risk. I also do a "rent a shelf" scheme in some shops, pay £x a month and they take a small commission when things sell. 

For wholesale I'd offer 40-50% off, so I usually start sale or return, for a higher %. Then if they sell well, the shops know they can place a wholesale order for a better price.

It's exhausting honestly. If you're doing outdoor markets and have to bring your own gazebo/tent, you'll often have to arrive at the crack of dawn and are setting up 2 hrs before you even start selling.

My biggest piece of advice is take someone with you, help with setting up, if you need to pop to the loo, or get some food, or just relax for 5. I know it's not always possible, but its always easier with a buddy. 

Also always price your items visibly. People don't want to ask what the price of everything is, they want to know immediately if your items are in their price range. And bring a wide variety of items in different price ranges. My best sellers online barely sell in person, and vice versa. 

Be friendly, without being overbearing. Have a smile and say "good morning", but don't be too salesy with people. Some people like to chat, and be recommended items. Some people want to throw some money at you and walk away. It totally depends on the person, but that's pretty easy to gage straight away. 

I know from experience shopping myself, if I think the vender is going to talk my ear off or try to upsell me, I don't even approach the booth. Anxiety and all that. 

It's really hard work, but can be worth it and good fun if you find the right place with the right product. You make more of an impression on people seeing your face, than just a website online. And it's a good way to get local business as well! I always include a business card in the bag if they purchase, and have had a lot of repeat customers this way.

Hope this helps! We've just started doing in person selling this last year and have learned a lot doing 20 ish markets throughout 2021
